FOREWORD

0.1This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 10 October 1985, after the draft finalized by the Brushware Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council.
0.2 Brushes, scrubbing are extensively used by the D:fence Services, Indian Railways and others. There is an increasing demand for these types of brushes for cleaning operations where scrubbing is necessary. Originally this specification was based on 25-61 `Indian Railway Standard Specification for brushes, hair, fibre and cane brushes. ( other than painters brushes )`, issued by the Ministry of Railways. 0.3 In this revision, three amendments issued to the earlier standard have been incorporated. Moreover, the tolerance limits specified have been rationalized on similar lines as in other similar brushware standards. Also the flat type of scrubbing brush extensively used, has been included in this revision. 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

IS :3015- 1985 4.1.6.2 The timber shall be reasonably straight-grained and wellseasoned to a moisture content not exceeding 15 percent when tested by the electronic moisture meter method. In case of dispute the oven-dry method shall be used ( see Appendix B ).
4.1.6.3 The timber shall be free from brashness any kind of decay ( rot ) insect attack, centre heart ( pith ), knots ( except live pin knots ), cracks, warp or any other defect which may reduce the life of the brush or affect its utility. 4.1.7 Wire Brass wire of 0'56 & 0'06 mm diameter shall be used. coated mild steel wire of 41.8 Staples - Bright iron or copper 0'80 f 0'1 mm diameter shall be used.

4.1.9 Nails - Steel nails 12 mm long and of 1'40 mm diameter shall be used for securing the back over the exposed portion of the brush.

4.3.4 Type A - Only staple setting of scrubbing brush flat is suitable and not wire-drawn. The tufts of filling material shall be firmly slogged into the knot-holes by machine cross stapling so that they cannot be easily withdrawn. The board shall then be finished smooth.

4.3.5 Type B - Scrubbing brush, winged shall be manufactured by wire-drawn or a staple setting.

either

4.3.5.1 For wire drawn brushes - The tufts of filling material shall be firmly drawn into the tuft holes by means of brass or bright iron wire and thorougly bottomed, so that they cannot be subsequently knocked back. The back shall be securely glued to the board and reinforced with 8 nails, as shown in Fig. 2, in such a manner that they do not foul the wire or the filling material.

4.3.5.2 The filling material shall be trimmed straight-faced shape of the brush as shown in Fig. 2.

to give the

4.3.5.3 Staple set brushes - No back is required. The tufts of filling material shall be firmly slogged into the knot holes by machine cross stapling so that they cannot be easily withdrawn. The board shall then be finished smooth. 6

MARKING 5.1 Unless otherwise agreed to between the indentor or inspection authority and the supplier, each brush shall be legibly and indelibly marked or stamped with the manufacturer's name or recognized trademark, if any, type and grade and the year of manufacture. 5.1.1 The brushes may also be marked with the IS1 Certification Mark.
NOTE - The use of the IS1 Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The IS1 Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard gnder a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer. IS1 marked products are also continuously checked by IS1 for conforDetails of conditions under which mity to that standard as a further safeguard. a licence for the use of the IS1 Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.

SAMPLING 7.1 The supplier shall submit three identical brushes for approval. 7.2 The indentor or inspection authority shall retain one of the three samples approved against each type and grade of brush, scrubbing, till the completion of the order.

TEST METHODS according to the methods prescribed in 8.1

8.0 Tests shall be conducted and 8.2.

8.1 Pull Test - The tufts of filling material shall not pull out when subjected to a straight pull between thumb and finger grip. 8.2 Mass of Filling Material for Finished Brush - Unfasten tufts by removal of fastening wire or staples. Determine the total mass of filling material. 8.2.1 The masses of filling material for each grade of brush, scrubbing, shall be as follows:
For Type A For Type B Grade 1 Grade 2 -

54 g of the medium stiff fibre.

54 g of the mixture for the body and snout and 18 g for the wings ( pure bassine 1, and
54 g mixture of soft and stiff bassine fibre for body and snout and 18 g of stiff bassine fibre for wings.

8.2.2 A tolerance of ~t5 percent shall be allowed on the combined weight of filling material of the body, snout and wings provided the average mass of the filling material per brush in any lot, is not below the specified value.
9. SHELF

LIFE

9.1 The brushes shall have a shelf life of one year from the date of manufacture, provided proper storage conditions are used and adequate precautions are taken for prescribing them as given in 4 of IS : 3451 ( Part 2 )-1975*.

APPENDIX B ( Clause 4.1.6.2 )
DETERMINATION B-l. B-l.1 TEST SPECIMEN OF MOISTURE CONTENT OF TIMBER

The entire block used in brush, scrubbing, may form the test specimen for the determination of moisture content, or a coupon cut from the test specimen may, as well, be used for moisture content determination. When for any reason additional determination of moisture content is required, separate samples shall be prepared from the sample material as is used in preparing the test specimens. Smaller specimens may be used when deemed necessary. The test shall be carried out immediately after cutting the specimen. B-2. PROCEDURE each test specimen. This specimen shall then be dried in a ventilated oven at a temperature of 105 f 2�C until the mass becomes constant between the successive weighings made at an interval of not less than one hour.
B-3. CALCULATION B-3.1 Moisture B-2.1 Weigh accurately

content ( expressed as Ml - MO a percentage of the oven-dry mass ) = 100 X Mo [Ml = initial mass in g of the test specimen, and MO = oven-dry mass in g of the test specimen.

APPENDIX
SAMPLING C-l. SAMPLING FOR BRUSHES,

C
SCRUBBING

( Clauses 7.3 and 7.4 >

C-l.1 Lot - In any consignment all the brushes of the same size and quality shall be divided into groups of 1 000 brushes or less and each such group shall constitute a let. Care shall be taken to ensure that brushes included in a lot do not differ in construction, as far as possible.

11

IS:3015 -1985 C-1.1.1 The conformity of the brushes in a lot to the requirements of this specification shall be ascertained for each lot separately. The number of brushes to be selected for this purpose shall be in accordance with co1 1 and 2 of Table 1. C-1.1.2 Ths brushes shall be selected at random. ness of selection, one of the following procedures use: To ensure randomis recommended for

a) If all the brushes in a lot are packed in one box, then starting from any brush, count them in any suitable order as 1, 2...... ..up to r and so on where r is the integral part of N/n ( N and n being the lot size and sample size respectively ). Every r th brush thus counted shall be withdrawn to constitute the sample. b) If the brushes in a lot are packed in more than one box, approximately equal number of brushes shall be packed up at random from as many boxes as possible so as to obtain the required number of brushes as specified in Table 1.
